The name "Avocado & Shea Hand Cream" could be misleading under 21 CFR 701.1(b) because the label names the product after two ingredients—avocado and shea—but does not list all ingredients, even though the cream contains more than just these two. The provision specifically addresses labeling that suggests inclusion of one or more ingredients when not all are present, which may constitute a misleading representation [2].

21 CFR 701.1(b) prohibits labeling a cosmetic with a name that implies the presence of certain ingredients (like avocado and shea) if those ingredients are not all included in the product, even though the full list of ingredients is stated elsewhere on the label [2]. This means the name "Avocado & Shea Hand Cream" may be misleading because it suggests the product contains only these two ingredients or implies a focus on them when other ingredients are also present. The misbranding occurs if the name suggests inclusion of one or more but not all ingredients, which is prohibited under this regulation [2].
